- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The comment-creation POST to `/issues/${PR_NUMBER}/comments` is marked idempotent via the `GH_RETRY_IDEMPOTENT=true` prefix.
  WHY: A retry after an accepted POST can create a duplicate comment, and `tests/test_workflow_gh_retry_fallback_contract.py:501-509` rejects the marker on resource-creating POSTs.
- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Marking the same comment-creation POST idempotent enables duplicate writes on retry.
  WHY: The contract test fails, and a retry of an accepted POST returns 201 each time.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Close the PR as not planned and re-issue its issue on the current base branch the way the unblock judge's `reissue` verdict does for `kind == "pr"`" (issue #6748, "Required behaviour" step 2). The issue's Where-it-wires-in section also points the reissue at `scripts/unblock_actions.py`'s `reissue` ops for a pull request.
  Expected change site: the `context.json` built in `_resolver_reissue_for_host_only_scope` (around the `jq -n --slurpfile pr ...` call) and the matching read in `scripts/unblock_actions.py::_context` plus the `Integration branch` insertion in `plan`.
  Evidence of absence: the new reissue path only feeds `source_issue_body` / `source_issue_labels` into `_context()`, so `pr_source_target_branch` is populated exclusively from the linked issue's `- Integration branch:` line. The host-only reissue never extracts the PR's actual base (`p.base.ref`) and never sets `pr_source_target_branch` when the linked issue lacks that line. `scripts/unblock_actions.py:447-450` only emits `- Integration branch: ...` when `ctx.get("pr_source_target_branch")` is truthy, and `implement.yml` falls back to the repository's default branch when the body has no `Integration branch:`. For a host-only PR that targets a non-default base (the original motivating case was a `claude/x` PR held in the merge train), the reissue lands on the default branch instead of the PR's current base, which contradicts step 2 of the required behaviour and silently misroutes the redo.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- HARDENING_SUGGESTION
  Location: the `git diff "${_ho_merge_base}" HEAD -- "${_ho_path}" > ...; head -n 200 ...; if [ ... -gt 200 ]; then printf '%s\n' "... (truncated at 200 lines)" ...` block inside the take-base comment builder.
  Issue: The 200-line truncation marker omits the original line count, so reviewers cannot tell whether a truncation dropped one line or thousands.
  Suggested minimal fix: capture the original line count in a variable and append `(truncated from N lines)` to the marker.
  Estimated lines changed: 2

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:747 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: A comment-creating POST is marked idempotent.
  WHY: The repository's executable contract forbids this combination, and retrying an accepted POST can produce a duplicate explanation comment on the PR; the required CI check is already red on the current head.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: The linked issue (#6748, required behaviour 2) requires that when a host-only conflicted path is in the PR's declared scope, the PR is "closed and re-issued … on the current base branch". The README the PR adds repeats this ("its change is re-issued on the current `<base>` branch as #<m>").
  Expected change site: scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh `_resolver_reissue_for_host_only_scope` — the re-issue context construction (jq at lines 678-695) — and scripts/unblock_actions.py `plan()` PR branch (lines 434-454).
  Evidence of absence: The PR's base branch (`reissue_base`, derived from `BASE_BRANCH` at scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:667) reaches the re-issue planner only as prose inside the verdict `instructions` string (line 702). The structured context.json built at lines 678-695 carries no base/integration-branch field, and `scripts/unblock_actions.py` adds a structured `- Integration branch:` line to the replacement issue body only when `pr_source_target_branch` is parsed from the linked issue's own body (scripts/unblock_actions.py:447-448). For a PR whose base is not the default branch and whose linked issue body has no `Integration branch:` line, the created re-issue issue carries no structured branch metadata, so `scripts/resolve_integration_ref.sh` (body-line parser, default-branch fallback) will route the re-issued implementation to the repository default branch instead of the PR's actual base — the branch the resolver's own PR comment claims the work was re-issued onto. Last run changed the dedup marker and comment posting in this same function but did not add the base metadata.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
